==============================================================================
CASE 1  Revoked certificate, intact bytes (the Nikon Z6 III case)
          source: Golaszewski et al., arXiv:2604.24890 / IACR ePrint 2026/804
==============================================================================

  A Nikon Z6 III signing certificate was revoked in November 2025.
  Six months later, on the same file:
      Adobe Inspect  -> reported the signature VALID
      Verifieddit    -> reported the file INVALID
      paper          -> "Neither conforming validator reports the revocation."

  Our lattice, in both validator postures:

  posture A — validator did not check (c2pa-rs default ocsp_fetch=false)
    state       : valid_revocation_unknown
    integrity   : VALID
    revocation  : unknown_skipped  (known=False)
    -> NOT ASSERTABLE
    message     : A provenance credential is present, the content matches what was signed, and the signer is on the trust list in use. Revocation was NOT checked. A revoked credential would look identical to a current one here.

  posture B — validator checked and found the revocation
    state       : revoked
    integrity   : REVOKED
    revocation  : revoked  (known=True)
    -> NOT ASSERTABLE
    message     : The credential that signed this content was revoked by its issuer. The bytes may be intact; the authority to vouch for them is withdrawn. Revocation was checked: the credential is revoked.

  Neither posture can be shown as a pass. Constraint V2 forbids it:
  VALID + unknown revocation is a measurement we declined to take.

CASE 2  Revoked is not Tampered
          source: Verifieddit hasFatalValidation() renders both as 'altered after signing'
==============================================================================

  revoked credential, bytes intact
    state       : revoked
    integrity   : REVOKED
    revocation  : revoked  (known=True)
    -> NOT ASSERTABLE
    message     : The credential that signed this content was revoked by its issuer. The bytes may be intact; the authority to vouch for them is withdrawn. Revocation was checked: the credential is revoked.

  hard binding mismatch, bytes changed
    state       : tampered
    integrity   : TAMPERED
    revocation  : unknown_skipped  (known=False)
    -> NOT ASSERTABLE
    message     : Content binding or signature verification failed. This does not establish when, why, or by whom content changed. Revocation was NOT checked. A revoked credential would look identical to a current one here.

  Two different facts, two different sentences. Telling a user their
  file was altered when the real problem is a withdrawn credential is a
  false statement about the content.

CASE 3  The authenticated fake
          source: Nemecek et al., arXiv:2603.02378 — 'No deployed system adjudicates between them.'
==============================================================================

  A VALID manifest asserts human authorship. The pixels carry an
  AI-generation watermark. No cryptography is broken; one permitted
  assertion was omitted.

  manifest(human) vs watermark(ai)
    outcome     : contradicted   (rule R3)
    value       : None
    contradiction: 'ai' per trustmark:com.adobe.trustmark.Q
    contradiction: 'human' per c2pa:manifest/urn:uuid:...
    message     : origin: CONTRADICTED. Signals of equal standing disagree — 'ai' per trustmark:com.adobe.trustmark.Q; 'human' per c2pa:manifest/urn:uuid:.... No rule resolves which is authoritative, so none is presented as the answer.

  MANIFEST and WATERMARK hold equal standing by design, so the
  disagreement is irreducible. We name both sides instead of picking a
  winner we have no authority to pick.

          source: Liang et al. arXiv:2304.02819 (61.22% FPR on TOEFL); Khvatskii et al. arXiv:2608.11256
==============================================================================

  manifest(human) vs classifier(ai, confidence=1.0)
    outcome     : supported   (rule R2)
    value       : 'human'

    outcome     : unsupported   (rule R5)
